West African Democracy Solidarity Network CDD Ghana (2022-2024)

description.narrative: 1) Establish a transnational network to mobilize and strengthen cooperation, solidarity, and knowledgesharing among diverse prodemocracy civil society organizations and other civic actors and voices in the countries of West Africa. 2) Produce knowledge to support evidencedriven prodemocracy advocacy and activism in the region [WADEMOS Knowledge Hub]. 3) Promote regionwide awareness and compliance with the ECOWAS Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance as well as other democracyrelevant regional/international instruments and obligations. 4) Mobilize and harness creative talents (artists, poets, musicians, comedians/ satirists, cartoonists, social media influencers, etc.), and creative resources to use their craft to promote democratic norms and values within the region [DEMOCrATIVES]. 5) Strengthen and enhance the status and visibility of young women in governance and democratic projects in the Region, including in civil society leadership and activism [WADEMOS NextGen]. The following outcomes are expected to be achieved from effective implementation of the program: A strengthened WADEMOS relationship with ECOWAS on the compliance of the Protocol on democracy and good governance. Creation of, and sustained activism by young people, women, voluntary groups and the creative industry in defense of democracy and the ECOWAS protocol on democracy and governance. Strengthened cooperation and coordination among diverse CSOs in the Region to protect democratic norms and values. Enhanced evidenceinformed advocacy and activism to counter push back on democratic backsliding.

Projektets övergripande mål är att mobilisera och samordna demokratiska aktörer för att vända den negativa utvecklingen och verka för att demokratiska normer och reformer i regionen försvaras och återupplivas. Engagemang med regionala organ och instrument kommer utgöra en viktig del i det arbetet.
Det föreslagna projektet har fem huvudmål: 1) Etablera ett transnationellt nätverk för att mobilisera och stärka samarbete, solidaritet och kunskapsdelning mellan civilsamhällesorganisationer, aktörer och röster i Västafrika 2) Främja opinion- och aktivism till gagn för demokrati i regionen genom kunskapsproduktion och kunskapsdelning 3) Främja allmänhetens kunskap kring regionala aktörers arbete med ECOWAS-protokollet om demokrati och gott styre, samt andra relevanta regionala/internationella instrument och åtaganden 4) Mobilisera kreativa personer (konstnärer, poeter, musiker, komiker, serietecknare, influencers etc.) inom regionen, och utbilda nästa generations demokratiförespråkare. Inom samma mål ingår även stöd till demokratiinriktade rörelser ledda av kvinnor och unga 5) Stärka och förbättra unga kvinnors status och synlighet i demokratiprojekt i regionen.

The overall objective of the program is to mobilize, coordinate, and leverage the collective power of pro-democracy actors, resources, and opportunities within the region, including engagements with regional bodies and instruments, to push back democratic erosion and advance, defend, and reinvigorate democratic norms and reforms in the Sub-region. In order to achieve this CDD-Ghana has proposed the following five specific objectives:
1) Establish a transnational network to mobilize and strengthen cooperation, solidarity, and knowledge-sharing among diverse prodemocracy civil society organizations and other civic actors and voices in the countries of West Africa
2) Produce knowledge to support evidence-driven pro-democracy advocacy and activism in the region [WADEMOS Knowledge Hub].
3) Promote region-wide awareness and compliance with the ECOWAS Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance as well as other democracy-relevant regional/international instruments and obligations.
4) Mobilize and harness creative talents (artists, poets, musicians, comedians/satirists, cartoonists, social media influencers, etc.), and creative resources to use their craft to promote democratic norms and values within the region [DEMOCrATIVES].
5) Strengthen and enhance the status and visibility of young women in governance and democratic projects in the Region, including in civil society leadership and activism [WADEMOS NextGen].

The WADEMOS Network was established with the fundamental belief that civil society plays a critical role in safeguarding democracy and good governance. However, across West Africa, many civil society organizations (CSOs) operate in isolation, facing significant challenges in coordination, resource mobilization, and policy influence. In general, there is little crossborder collective action or solidarity among democracypromoting CSOs or among the regions CSOs generally in the areas of advocacy or activism. Recognizing these barriers, WADEMOS sought to mobilize, coordinate, and strengthen collaboration among diverse CSOs, fostering a unified front against democratic erosion. 6 (20) Avslutspromemoria Completion Memo Contribution ID: 15188 During the oneyear implementation period, the results achieved are related to laying the foundation for the network. Regional frameworks needed to be lobbied to work together and as a result high profile ECOWAS, AU, and UN officials made four profound statements endorsing WADEMOS and indicated their institutions willingness to work with the Network. Thus the key for the achievement of all the objectives of WADEMOS was successfully done. Since its official launch in September 2022, the size of the Network has grown exponentially, even at the launching event twice the number targeted, 35 CSOs participated. Bringingtogether relevant actors and creating the platform and facilitation by itself could be mentioned as a early season success. High profile individuals in the subregion have been identified and were contacted to fill the position of Advisory Council, out of which 4 accepted and contributed in advIsory roles. These are some of the foundational activities undertaken which contributed a lot to the success of WADEMOS. Stable Network To ensure sustained engagement, the WADEMOS Network also include a broader range of prodemocracy actors such as womenled groups, youth organizations, human rights defenders, and creatives. This inclusive approach helped amplify diverse voices within the movement, ensuring a more representative and impactful coalition. WADEMOS expanded its network from 35 to 60 Network Members. Alignment with Regional Democratic Challenges The relevance of WADEMOS is evident in its clear alignment with pressing challenges, serving as a regional platform to counter antidemocratic trends using channels of advocacy, capacitybuilding, and civil society mobilization. For instance, in countries like Mali, Burkina Faso, and Guinea, recent military coups have undermined democratic governance, resulting in governance gaps and decreased citizens enjoyment of their rights and liberties. WADEMOS work in promoting regional collaboration among CSOs addresses these issues directly through advocacy for the adherence to democratic norms and values, monitoring of the transition framework to ensure accountability, as well as regional governance frameworks such as the ECOWAS Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance. Alignment with ECOWAS and AU Democratic Governance Norms WADEMOS supports the implementation of the ECOWAS Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance the African Union Charter on Human and People Right 7 (20) Avslutspromemoria Completion Memo Contribution ID: 15188 Reporting mechanisms and other regional governance standards. The Network has also collaborated with these organisations on some programs and forums. Complementarity with other regional ProDemocracy Actors The project tends to build on the work of other democracycentred organisations, including the West Africa Network for Peacebuilding (WANEP) and the Media Foundation for West Africa (MfWA)all of which are part of the WADEMOS Network. WADEMOS, for example, engages in electoral observations and integrity discussions as well as events by providing insights into electoral risks and manipulations, thereby strengthening regional election monitoring efforts and complementing ECOWAS election observation missions. Coherence across countrylevel interventions Although WADEMOS operates across multiple countries with different democratic experiences, there is a coherent framework that ensures consistency across contexts while allowing for specific adaptations. An aspect of WADEMOS operation that ensures multicountry coherence lies in its ability to maintain a core strategic framework of thematic priorities while ensuring adaptability to local contexts. The project incorporates countryspecific advocacy and intervention strategies yet enables knowledgesharing across countries and ensuring that lessons learned in one context can inform developments in other locations. For instance, in countries where democratic institutions are relatively stable, the project focuses on strengthening proactive civil engagement, whereas, in countries with deteriorating democratic norms, WADEMOS prioritizes crisis response strategies and advocacy against unconstitutional rule. Summary of Results and Achievements I. A functioning Steering Committee (SC) II. Increased name recognition of WADEMOS and growing unsolicited interest in membership of the Network and participation in activities of the Network from civil society groups and civic formations in the Region. III. Recognition, acceptance, and endorsement of WADEMOS by leadership of the ECOWAS Commission and AU, and invitations for WADEMOS participation in dialogue, meetings, and other activities of the ECOWAS. IV. Successful deployment of incountry, preelection WADEMOS solidarity missions and stakeholder engagements in support of credible and peaceful elections in countries holding general elections 8 (20) Avslutspromemoria Completion Memo Contribution ID: 15188 V. Successful regional convening bringing together both civil society and ECOWAS to deliberate on democracy trends in the subregion and explore partnerships for solution. Two regional convening sessions were organized to advance this agenda: • Civil Society conference and outcome document on the State of Democracy in WA at the Annual Network Members Conference • Regional conference and release of outcome statement on democracy decline and Unconstitutional Changes of Government in francophone West Africa VI. Commissioned expert country study reports to guide CSO response and interventions in relation to the political transitions in countries under military rule VII. Targeted regional campaign on Tackling Presidential Term Extension and Violation of Human Rights and Freedoms in Senegal and West Africa to stimulate and mobilize demand for review of the ECOWAS supplementary protocol on democracy and good governance VIII. Successfully secured two additional grants from the Open Society Africa Office and the National Endowment for Democracy (NED) on Term limit in West Africa and political transitions IX. Successfully held strategy meeting with Creatives to explore collaborative partnerships and raise awareness and understanding on the state of democracy in West Africa and opportunities for Creatives to engage meaningfully in the democratic processes. X. Successfully implemented the Next Generation Initiative to empower young democrats and activists in West Africa XI. DEMOSFund operational and functional supporting timesensitive mobilization and initiatives in support of advocacy and activism in the subregion. XII.
